Write TWO test files (create test/ if needed): /root/bench-runs/h6-b61c9e99/test/patch-ops.test.mjs (operations + apply failures) and /root/bench-runs/h6-b61c9e99/test/patch-copy.test.mjs (immutability, no-sharing, -0, member order, test-op equality). Do NOT edit jsonpatch.mjs or anything else. Node v22, node:test + node:assert/strict only. Run each with `node --test test/<file>` (plain commands, no `;`/`&&` chaining). Each file under ~380 lines; small helpers OK (e.g. `expectPatchError(doc, patch, message, index)` checking err instanceof PatchError, err.name==='PatchError', message and index EXACT). Always exact equality; for member order assert `assert.deepStrictEqual(Object.keys(result), [...])`; for -0 use `Object.is(x, -0)` assertions (deepStrictEqual distinguishes -0 too). No console.log. If a test fails, do NOT weaken it: report input/expected/actual and jsonpatch.mjs line.

Import: `import { applyPatch, PatchError } from '../jsonpatch.mjs';`

== patch-ops.test.mjs ==
- add: path "" replaces whole doc ({"a":1} add "" value [1] -> [1]; add "" value 5 on any -> 5). Else follow parent; object: new member appended per order rule, existing member keeps its place ({"a":1,"b":2} add /a 9 -> keys ["a","b"], value 9). Array: "-" appends ([1,2] add /- 3 -> [1,2,3]); index <= length inserts ([1,2] add /0 0 -> [0,1,2]; add /2 3 -> [1,2,3] (index == length OK); add /3 -> `operation 0: path not found`). add /01, /+1, /1.0, /x, / (empty token) on array -> `bad index`. add on parent that is string/number/bool/null: {"s":"x"} add /s/0 -> path not found; {"z":null} add /z/a -> path not found. add with missing parent {"a":{}} add /b/c -> path not found; parent path through array with bad index {"a":[1]} add /a/x/y -> bad index; through "-" {"a":[1]} add /a/-/y -> path not found. add "/" on {} -> {"":v}. add /__proto__ on {} -> result has OWN property "__proto__" (Object.hasOwn true), Object.getPrototypeOf(result) === Object.prototype, keys ["__proto__"]. Add value null works.
- remove: path must name a value: {"a":1,"b":2} remove /a -> {"b":2}; [1,2,3] remove /1 -> [1,3]; remove /3 on [1,2,3] -> path not found; remove /- -> path not found; remove /01 -> bad index; remove /x on {} -> path not found; remove JSON.parse('{"__proto__":1,"a":2}') /__proto__ -> {"a":2} with no own __proto__.
- replace: "" whole doc; else must name a value; member keeps place ({"a":1,"b":2,"c":3} replace /b 9 -> keys ["a","b","c"]); [1,2] replace /1 9 -> [1,9]; replace /2 on [1,2] -> path not found; replace /- -> path not found; replace /x on {} -> path not found (replace must not create); replace /0x on array -> bad index.
- move: from must name a value: missing from -> `operation 0: from not found`; from bad index on array -> `bad index`. Removed then added at path, array index counts after removal: [1,2,3] move from /0 path /2 -> [2,3,1]; [1,2,3] move from /0 to /3 -> path not found (after removal length 2). {"a":1,"b":2} move /a -> /c -> keys ["b","c"]. from === path -> no-op once from found ({"a":1,"b":2} move /a to /a -> same, keys order ["a","b"]); move from /missing to /missing -> from not found. move follows from first: {} move from /x path /y/z -> `from not found` (not path not found). move from /a path /b/c where /b missing on {"a":1} -> path not found. move up: {"a":{"b":1}} from /a/b path /a -> {"a":1}.
- copy: deep copy of from taken before change, added at path; path may lie inside from: {"a":{"b":1}} copy /a -> /a/c -> {"a":{"b":1,"c":{"b":1}}}; result.a.c !== result.a; copy from missing -> from not found; copy follows from first ({} copy from /x path /y/z -> from not found); copy into array [1,2] from /0 to /- -> [1,2,1].
- test: path "" = whole doc; failure -> `test failed`; test on missing path -> path not found (not test failed); test /- on array -> path not found.
- Apply in order: later op sees earlier result ([{add /a 1},{test /a 1},{replace /a 2},{test /a 2}]); failure at op 2 reports `operation 2: <reason>` index 2.
- applyPatch throws only PatchError: a few failing cases each check instanceof PatchError.

== patch-copy.test.mjs ==
- Never changes doc or patch, also when it throws: build doc/patch, take structuredClone snapshots, run success and failing patches (failure at the LAST op after earlier ops add/remove/replace/move mutated things), then deepStrictEqual against snapshots. Also Object.freeze deeply the doc and patch (recursive freeze helper) and run a patch with add/remove/replace/move/copy: must not throw TypeError.
- Result shares no object/array with doc or patch: patch [] returns deep copy (result !== doc, result.a !== doc.a, nested arrays too, deepStrictEqual equal). add value object: result.x !== patch[0].value, and mutating result afterwards does not change patch value. replace value same. Write a helper collecting all objects in result and in doc+patch (iterative walk) and assert empty intersection for a mixed patch.
- Numbers kept exactly: {"a":-0} with [] -> Object.is(result.a, -0); add value -0 -> -0 kept; replace -0; copy of -0 keeps -0; move keeps -0; array [-0] kept; 1e308, 5e-324, 0.1, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+2 kept exactly.
- Member order (Object.keys order: integer-index names first ascending, then insertion): add /1 = 5 to {"b":0} gives keys ["1","b"] and deepStrictEqual {"1":5,"b":0}; {"b":0,"a":1} add /c -> ["b","a","c"]; add /__proto__ to {"b":0} -> keys ["b","__proto__"]; doc JSON.parse('{"z":1,"__proto__":{"x":1},"a":2}') with [] -> keys ["z","__proto__","a"], result own __proto__ value deepStrictEqual {"x":1}, Object.getPrototypeOf(result)===Object.prototype, and result.__proto__ value is not doc's object; replace /__proto__ keeps place; copy into "__proto__" name works; remove then add re-appends at end ({"a":1,"b":2}: remove /a, add /a 1 -> keys ["b","a"]).
- test equality: same JSON type; numbers by value (1 vs 1.0 equal, 0 vs -0 equal both ways); 1 vs "1" fails; strings exact ("é" "é" vs "é" -> test failed; "a" vs "a " fails; "A" vs "a" fails); arrays same length and order ([1,2] vs [2,1] fails; [1] vs [1,1] fails; [] vs {} fails; {} vs [] fails); objects same names any order ({"a":1,"b":2} vs {"b":2,"a":1} passes; {"a":1} vs {"a":1,"b":2} fails; {"a":1,"b":2} vs {"a":1} fails; {"a":undefined}? skip); true/false/null only themselves (null vs false, null vs 0, null vs {}, null vs [], false vs 0, true vs 1, "" vs false, 0 vs "" all fail; null vs null pass); nested deep equality passes/fails at depth; object with __proto__ member: doc JSON.parse('{"__proto__":1}') vs value JSON.parse('{"__proto__":1}') pass, vs {} fail; doc {} vs value JSON.parse('{"__proto__":1}')? fail. Every failure message exactly `operation 0: test failed`.

Load the skill tdd-workflow with the Skill tool if available (otherwise ignore). Report: file paths, test counts, pass/fail summary, any failure details.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.
